doc.title: Dick Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Emerson Brown portrayed
summary: Sherman describes Emerson Brown as difficult but passionate, tells of the pawned moose head in Syracuse and a night of brushes and clarinet, and a long bike ride.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: That about sums him up I guess.

Emerson had his drawbacks personality-wise. He was difficult to deal with and I as the leader would try to recruit him every year to play Hamilton reunions and it was like pulling teeth. He wanted to play. He loved playing. But he just put me through a wringer all the time. I would say, “If you can’t make it just say no and I’ll get someone else.” He would keep dragging it out.
He made you work for it.
He made me work for it.

He had failings. As a leader he was impatient. He didn’t look around to see if the drummer’s got drumsticks in his hand. He was just too eager to go. But all that aside, nobody liked to play more than he or had more passion for playing than he. So he deserves high marks for that because he inspired everybody around him. He drove himself and he drove the band, so he was a good man. I understand that his widow may be attending.
She’s supposed to be here tonight actually. I’m doing an alumni college.

I’ve know her very well for a long — many, many years. One time I drove up to see Emerson and Cindy, who were living in Syracuse at that time, and they were low on funds and they had a big moose that was hanging on the wall, a moose head. And they took it out and they hocked the moose head so we could buy a steak.

And then we spent that night at the window of Emerson’s apartment, it was on the third floor. The snowflakes were swirling down and I was playing on a snare drum with brushes and he was playing the clarinet out the window. That was the band.
Didn’t he used to take a long bike ride?
Oh he rode up from Nashville one time on a bike. His wife would come along with him and they’d stop and eat and she would take care of him.
Oh yeah, that’s a remarkable thing.
